author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Senator Rick Scott discusses affordability and business climate in Florida with Wall Street Journal
text:
Senator Rick Scott discussed Florida’s recent unemployment figures and efforts to address the state’s affordability challenges during an interview with Arian Campo-Florez of the Wall Street Journal, according to a May 20 statement.
The conversation focused on what steps Florida can take to become more attractive for businesses. Scott said, “How can Florida become the state that everybody wants to do business with? Lower taxes, lower fees, a well-educated workforce, a regulatory environment that makes sense… That’s [step] number one.”
Scott champions fiscal responsibility, debt reduction and policies supporting families and small businesses, according to the official website . He serves on several Senate committees including Armed Services, Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, Budget and the Special Committee on Aging.
Before his political career, Scott served on active duty in the U.S. Navy aboard the USS Glover after high school. He earned a business degree from the University of Missouri-Kansas City and a law degree from Southern Methodist University. Scott won election to represent Florida in the U.S. Senate; he and his wife Ann raised two daughters together and enjoy time with their grandchildren—all according to his official website .
The interview comes as policymakers continue looking for solutions to economic issues affecting Floridians. The discussion highlighted priorities such as tax policy, education, workforce development and regulation.
